title: Patterned Wafer Inspection - Voids Detection on Teron 640
subtitle: Post-Deposition Quality Validation for 28nm Node Manufacturing
author: Dr. Thomas Mueller

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Teron 640 system to detect and classify Voids defects during post-deposition inspection at the 28nm technology node. The test is conducted at Hsinchu Fab 15 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 200mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Voids defects that are critical to yield at the 28nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Teron 640 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Teron 640
- Inspection Type: Patterned Wafer Inspection
- Target Defect: Voids
- Process Step: Post-Deposition
- Wafer Size: 200mm
- Technology Node: 28nm
- Fab Location: Hsinchu Fab 15

This test case applies to all Teron 640 systems deployed at Hsinchu Fab 15 for post-deposition monitoring in the 28nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Teron 640
Software Version: v8.2.363
Recipe: PATTERNED_WAFER_INSPECTION_28nm_POST_DEPOSITION
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: Medium (179 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.5μm
Edge Exclusion: 2mm
Sampling Plan: Full wafer sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Teron 640 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Patterned Wafer Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Voids defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 28nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 57 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 93% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±1.0% for Patterned Wafer Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.98 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-11-30
Wafers Tested: 28
Total Defects Found: 4955
Defect Density: 1577.23 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 3.5%
Capture Rate: 96.6%
Test Duration: 406 minutes
System Uptime: 97.1%

Result Classification: CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Teron 640 demonstrated acceptable performance in detecting Voids at the 28nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate is within acceptable limits.

d) Cross-correlation with the reference SEM confirmed classification accuracy.

e) SECS/GEM communication was verified with zero packet loss during data transfer.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Review edge-zone detection parameters for optimization.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Monitor performance over next 30 production days.
